metrics.label: Brent crude

metrics.label: WTI crude

metrics.label: Dutch TTF gas

metrics.label: Henry Hub gas

metrics.label: Coal API2 (ARA)

metrics.label: Heating oil / gasoil

metrics.label: RBOB gasoline

metrics.label: Dry bulk ETF (BDRY)

metrics.blurb: An ETF holding tanker freight futures. A rough daily read on tanker sentiment.

metrics.label: Baltic Capesize Index
metrics.blurb: The Capesize component of the Baltic Dry Index. The most volatile part, and effectively a bet on Chinese steel production.

metrics.label: Baltic Panamax Index
metrics.blurb: The Panamax component. Coal and grain rather than iron ore, so it follows harvests and power demand more than steel.

metrics.label: Baltic Supramax Index
metrics.blurb: The Supramax component. These ships have their own cranes and serve smaller ports, so it reflects broad trade rather than one commodity.

metrics.label: Baltic Dry Index
metrics.blurb: The Baltic Exchange's headline dry bulk freight index. Published late afternoon London time, so a morning brief shows the previous session.

metrics.label: VLSFO Singapore
metrics.blurb: Price of the main low-sulphur marine fuel at the world's biggest bunker port.

metrics.label: VLSFO Rotterdam
metrics.blurb: The same fuel in Europe's biggest bunker port.

metrics.label: VLSFO Fujairah
metrics.blurb: The Middle East bunker hub, where most VLCC voyages refuel.

metrics.label: Diesel crack vs Brent
metrics.blurb: Roughly what a refinery makes turning a barrel of crude into diesel. Computed as the gasoil price converted to barrels minus Brent. Fat margins make refineries run hard, which creates product tanker cargo.

metrics.label: Brent–WTI spread
metrics.blurb: How much more Brent costs than WTI. A wide gap makes exporting US crude profitable, which means more long-haul cargoes and stronger tanker demand.

rates.label: VLCC (TD3C, AG→China)

rates.label: Aframax (TD7, N.Sea→UKC)

brief.text:
The most important item in today's data is not a price but a headline: Seatrade Maritime reports a seafarer fatality in a Gulf tanker attack and a VLCC — a Very Large Crude Carrier, the biggest standard crude tanker, around two million barrels — struck in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran said to be widening both the area of attacks and the types of vessel targeted. For anyone fixing ships, that is a war-risk and crew-safety question before it is a rate question: owners may decline Arabian Gulf business, and insurers reprice it.

On today's figures, Brent crude is $98.32 a barrel, down 12 cents (-0.1%), and WTI is $90.34, down 18 cents (-0.2%), with the Brent–WTI spread at $7.98. Bunkers — the fuel ships burn — rose at all four hubs today: VLSFO (very low sulphur fuel oil) is $865.00 a tonne in Fujairah, up $13.50 (+1.6%), $854.00 in Singapore (+$4.50), $770.50 in Houston, up $16.50 (+2.2%), and $739.50 in Rotterdam (+$7.50). Bunkers rising while crude eases is not explained by anything in this data. The diesel crack against Brent is $84.09 today. No freight benchmark has refreshed: the Baltic Dry Index stood at 2,805 points on Friday 6 November, up 65 (+2.4%), the Baltic Capesize Index — Capesizes are the largest dry bulk ships, typically iron ore and coal — was 4,097 on Wednesday 4 November, and the VLCC TD3C Gulf-to-China TCE, the daily earnings a voyage leaves an owner after voyage costs, was $1,345,710 a day on Sunday 1 November.

Running stories: Hormuz attacks developed today with the reported fatality and VLCC strike. Sanctions on the shadow fleet also moved — gCaptain reports the US blocking five Cuban-flagged vessels — and ARACON heard that a quarter of the internationally trading crude fleet now sits on the dark list. Black Sea drone attacks, US and European port labour, Russian diesel export curbs and chokepoint transit counts had no fresh news today and are unchanged. LNG Prime reports Atlantic and Pacific spot LNG rates rose for a third week.

Watch two things. First, whether Baltic tanker and dry assessments refresh after the weekend, since nothing has printed since Friday at best. Second, whether further Hormuz incidents are reported, given today's widening of targets.

storylines.title: Direct attacks on ships in Hormuz
storylines.what: Attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz have continued into November. Today a seafarer was killed in a Gulf tanker attack and a VLCC was struck in Hormuz, with Iran reported to be widening both the geographic area of attacks and the vessel types targeted.
storylines.why_it_matters: Crew fatalities and hull strikes raise war-risk premiums and crew-safety objections for Arabian Gulf liftings, shrinking the pool of willing owners and supporting crude and product tanker earnings.
storylines.latest: First reported seafarer fatality in a Gulf tanker attack, plus a VLCC struck in Hormuz and a reported widening of targeting.
sources: Seafarer fatality in Gulf tanker attack, VLCC struck in Hormuz

storylines.title: Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab transits and Gulf congestion
storylines.what: Strait of Hormuz traffic rose in October to its highest monthly level since July, supported by dry bulk and LNG movements even as VLCC traffic declined. Red Sea traffic also rose and Arabian Gulf waiting remains elevated.
storylines.why_it_matters: Transit counts and waiting times show whether ships route through or around high-risk waters, changing voyage lengths, tonne-mile demand and effective fleet supply.
sources: Seafarer fatality in Gulf tanker attack, VLCC struck in Hormuz

storylines.title: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet
storylines.what: The US has expanded sanctions on Cuba's maritime and energy sectors, identifying five Cuban-flagged vessels as blocked property and opening the door to sanctions on foreign companies dealing with them, following earlier action against Iranian false-flag registry networks. Analysts now say a quarter of the internationally trading crude fleet sits on the dark list.
storylines.why_it_matters: Registry fraud, AIS spoofing and blocked-property designations force charterers, insurers and class societies to re-verify documentation and positions, and push tonnage out of mainstream trades, tightening compliant tanker supply.
storylines.latest: US sanctions on five Cuban-flagged vessels; ARACON told the dark fleet has tripled since 2022 and covers 25% of the trading crude fleet.
sources: U.S. Targets Cuba’s Oil Tanker Fleet in New Sanctions Crackdown
ARACON: 25% of the internationally-trading crude oil fleet now sits on the dark list

storylines.title: Drone attacks on shipping in the western Black Sea
storylines.what: A Greek container ship sank after being hit by naval drones off Bulgaria, the latest in a series of strikes in the western Black Sea.
storylines.why_it_matters: Attacks on ships and port infrastructure threaten grain and dry bulk loadings from the region and add insurance and routing costs for any vessel calling there.
sources: Webinar: Navigating the danger zone: How to protect your fleet from GPS attacks

storylines.title: Russian diesel flows and export restrictions
storylines.what: A reported US-Russia agreement on supplying extra diesel to the US market has met political opposition, while Russia has extended a general ban on most diesel exports until the end of January, with some volumes still allowed to flow.
storylines.why_it_matters: Diesel export restrictions and any reopened Atlantic route reshape clean product tanker ton-miles and MR and LR employment patterns.
sources: ARACON: 25% of the internationally-trading crude oil fleet now sits on the dark list

storylines.title: Port labour disruption in the US and Europe
storylines.what: A contract standoff involving 250 security workers threatens to freeze operations across Los Angeles and Long Beach terminals after a 4 November deadline extension, while dockworkers struck across Europe and beyond over arms shipments.
storylines.why_it_matters: Labour action at container and ferry berths disrupts berthing schedules and cargo flows, and the unresolved US West Coast dispute leaves a large share of US import capacity exposed to stoppage.

storylines.title: Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab transits and Gulf congestion
storylines.what: Strait of Hormuz traffic rose in October to its highest monthly level since July, supported by dry bulk and LNG movements even as VLCC traffic declined. Red Sea traffic also rose and Arabian Gulf waiting remains elevated.
storylines.why_it_matters: Transit counts and waiting times show whether ships route through or around high-risk waters, changing voyage lengths, tonne-mile demand and effective fleet supply.
sources: Seafarer fatality in Gulf tanker attack, VLCC struck in Hormuz

storylines.title: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet
storylines.what: The US has expanded sanctions on Cuba's maritime and energy sectors, identifying five Cuban-flagged vessels as blocked property and opening the door to sanctions on foreign companies dealing with them, following earlier action against Iranian false-flag registry networks. Analysts now say a quarter of the internationally trading crude fleet sits on the dark list.
storylines.why_it_matters: Registry fraud, AIS spoofing and blocked-property designations force charterers, insurers and class societies to re-verify documentation and positions, and push tonnage out of mainstream trades, tightening compliant tanker supply.
storylines.latest: US sanctions on five Cuban-flagged vessels; ARACON told the dark fleet has tripled since 2022 and covers 25% of the trading crude fleet.
sources: U.S. Targets Cuba’s Oil Tanker Fleet in New Sanctions Crackdown
ARACON: 25% of the internationally-trading crude oil fleet now sits on the dark list

storylines.title: Drone attacks on shipping in the western Black Sea
storylines.what: A Greek container ship sank after being hit by naval drones off Bulgaria, the latest in a series of strikes in the western Black Sea.
storylines.why_it_matters: Attacks on ships and port infrastructure threaten grain and dry bulk loadings from the region and add insurance and routing costs for any vessel calling there.
sources: Webinar: Navigating the danger zone: How to protect your fleet from GPS attacks

storylines.title: Russian diesel flows and export restrictions
storylines.what: A reported US-Russia agreement on supplying extra diesel to the US market has met political opposition, while Russia has extended a general ban on most diesel exports until the end of January, with some volumes still allowed to flow.
storylines.why_it_matters: Diesel export restrictions and any reopened Atlantic route reshape clean product tanker ton-miles and MR and LR employment patterns.
sources: ARACON: 25% of the internationally-trading crude oil fleet now sits on the dark list

storylines.title: Port labour disruption in the US and Europe
storylines.what: A contract standoff involving 250 security workers threatens to freeze operations across Los Angeles and Long Beach terminals after a 4 November deadline extension, while dockworkers struck across Europe and beyond over arms shipments.
storylines.why_it_matters: Labour action at container and ferry berths disrupts berthing schedules and cargo flows, and the unresolved US West Coast dispute leaves a large share of US import capacity exposed to stoppage.
sources: Adani Ports Makes Major Push Into Europe With $2.9 Billion Evos Acquisition
